html:
Lake Assal is a crater lake in central Djibouti, about 155 metres below sea level, the lowest point in Africa, whose salt flats have long been worked by the Afar.

It is one of the saltiest bodies of water in the world. For centuries Afar herders cut its salt and carried it by camel caravan inland to the markets of the Ethiopian highlands, where salt bars were even used as money.

Salt is still mined there, now partly for export by sea. The lake lies in the Afar rift, where Africa is slowly pulling apart, and draws visitors and scientists to Djibouti. It recalls the old caravan links that the railway later replaced.
sum: Lake Assal is a crater lake in central Djibouti, about 155 metres below sea level, the lowest point in Africa, whose salt flats have long been worked by the Afar.
